info.title: wallet-backend API
info.description:
wallet-backend is a non-custodial Base (EVM L2) wallet backend: user/wallet management, payments, swaps, shared-access multisig wallets, KYC, fiat/crypto on-off ramps, market making, asset tokenization, subscriptions, partner integrations (servicelinks), and wallet recovery.

## Authentication

Most user-facing routes use **SignatureAuth**: the caller signs `fullPathWithQuery + signerAddress + timestamp` with their own private key (personal_sign/EIP-191) and presents the result via four headers - `X-Signer-Address`, `X-Wallet-Address`, `X-Signature`, `X-Timestamp`. There is no session or bearer token for ordinary user operations; every request is independently signed and verified offline. `X-Wallet-Address` is the wallet the request acts on - it equals `X-Signer-Address` for an undeployed/bare identity, or a Safe smart-contract wallet address the signer owns or has a delegated `sharedaccess` role on otherwise. The signature is checked against a server-configured clock-drift tolerance (`SIGNATURE_AUTH_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`), which is the only replay defense in this scheme.

Partner-integration routes (`/v1/partner/...`) use **ApiKeyAuth**: a raw API key in the `X-API-Key` header, issued per partner integration (a `ServiceLink`) via the admin surface.

Admin routes and the servicelinks partner-login session use **BearerAuth**: a JWT in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, scoped by an `aud` (audience) claim - `admin` for the admin surface, a servicelinks-specific audience for a partner login session token issued by the QR-login/approval flow. The two audiences are not interchangeable even though both use this same scheme.

A handful of routes are genuinely public (health check, curated asset listings, published announcements/reference data, shortlink redirects, and the Branch A/B account-recovery execution routes, which are gated by an emailed OTP plus security questions instead of a request signature since the caller has - by definition - lost access to their signing key).

## Error shape

Every non-2xx response uses the same envelope, regardless of which example schema an individual operation below shows:

```json
{"error": "bad_request", "message": "human-readable detail"}
```

`error` is a short machine-readable code (see `internal/apperrors`); `message` is a human-readable detail string safe to display or log.

## Networks

This spec describes the API shape, which is identical on Base Sepolia (testnet) and Base mainnet - only the server you point at differs (see `DEPLOYMENT.md` §2). Addresses, chain IDs, and transaction hashes returned by a given deployment are native to whichever network that deployment runs against.

get.description: Returns the active entries in the wallet's curated ERC-20 token catalog (the list shown in a token picker), not the full set of ERC-20 tokens an address might hold. Unlike Stellar trustlines, Base/EVM has no on-chain opt-in gating which assets an address can hold, so this catalog is purely an app-side curation concern layered on top of an otherwise permissionless balance model. Public, unauthenticated endpoint.

get.summary: Get an address's native or token balance
get.description: Returns the balance of the given address in the smallest unit (wei for native ETH, or the token's base unit) as a decimal string, avoiding floating-point precision loss. Omit the `token` query parameter for the native ETH balance, or pass an ERC-20 contract address to read that token's balance instead. Both `address` and an optional `token` are validated as well-formed EVM addresses before the chain is queried. Public, unauthenticated endpoint.

post.summary: Build an unsigned ERC-20 approve transaction
post.description: Returns an unsigned EIP-1559 `approve(spender, amount)` transaction for the caller's wallet to sign completely offline - the EVM template's equivalent of a Stellar trustline build. `amount` is a decimal integer string in the token's base unit, not a human-readable amount. The owner is taken from the verified `X-Wallet-Address` subject rather than the request body, so the built transaction always spends the authenticated caller's own allowance. An optional `nonce` supports offline-batched signing.

post.summary: Submit a client-signed payment and record its history
post.description: Broadcasts a client-signed native ETH or ERC-20 transfer to the chain and records it in payment history, keyed by a caller-supplied `idempotencyKey`. Because signing can happen long after build, an app's natural retry-on-reconnect behavior means the same signed transaction may be submitted more than once; resubmitting the same `idempotencyKey` returns the original stored record rather than erroring or creating a duplicate history entry. A network-rejected submission (bad nonce, insufficient funds, etc.) triggers an operational alert and a 400 response.
